gilmoretyrannus:eswiki:7.title: Nanotyrannus (Controversia: T. rex inmaduro o género separado)

facts.statement: The type locality of Gilmoretyrannus is the Lance and Hell Creek formations.
facts.quote: Type locality: Lance and Hell Creek formations

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus was described by Sancarlo and Paul.
facts.quote: Authors: Sancarlo & Paul

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus fossils were found in the United States.
facts.quote: Country: United States

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus fossils were found in the regions of Montana and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Region: Montana, Wyoming

facts.statement: Gilmoretyrannus is a newly proposed genus and combination.
facts.quote: Novelty: Gen. et comb. nov

facts.statement: The type species of Gilmoretyrannus is Nanotyrannus lethaeus, described by Zanno and Napoli in 2025.
facts.quote: The type species is Nanotyrannus lethaeus Zanno & Napoli (2025).

facts.statement: The fossil range of Nanotyrannus is the Late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Maastrichtian

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was established by Bakker, Williams, and Currie in 1988.
facts.quote: authority: Bakker, Williams & Currie, 1988

facts.statement: The type species of Nanotyrannus was originally described by Gilmore in 1946.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Gilmore, 1946

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived in western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 67 million years ago.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus (/ˈnænoʊˌtaɪˌrænəs, -tɪ- /, ) is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur that lived in what is now western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, 67 million years ago.

facts.statement: In 1988, Bakker, Williams, and Currie moved the species to the new genus Nanotyrannus, referencing its small body size.
facts.quote: Re-examination of the specimen in 1988 by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams and Philip J. Currie moved the species to a new genus of tyrannosaurid, named Nanotyrannus in reference to its small body size compared to other tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is based on skull CMNH 7541, collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus is based on CMNH 7541, a skull collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.

facts.statement: It was described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore as a new species in the genus Gorgosaurus, G. lancensis.
facts.quote: It was described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore, who classified it as a new species in the tyrannosaurid genus Gorgosaurus, G. lancensis.

facts.statement: In 1988, the specimen was re-described by Bakker, Williams, and Currie at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: In 1988, the specimen was re-described by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams, then the curator of paleontology at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History, and Phil Currie, where the original specimen was housed and is now on display.

facts.statement: The etymology of Nanotyrannus is derived from the Greek words nanos (dwarf or pygmy) and tyrannos (king).
facts.quote: The etymology has subsequently been clarified to be derived from the Greek words νάνος (nanos), meaning dwarf or pygmy, and τύραννος (tyrannos), meaning king.

facts.statement: Analysis by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated the specimen was immature, leading many paleontologists to consider it a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Subsequent analysis of the specimen by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated that it was immature, leading Carr and many other paleontologists to consider it a juvenile specimen of T. rex.

facts.statement: The fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020.
facts.quote: The fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020, after which the museum built an additional research lab space in which to prepare, study, and display the specimens.

facts.statement: The taxonomic status of Nanotyrannus has been a subject of intense scientific debate, with many researchers favoring its identification as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Subsequent research indicated that the skull belonged to an immature animal, leading many researchers to favor its identification as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex. Its taxonomic status has since been a subject of intense scientific debate.

facts.statement: An independent study by Griffin et al. argued the holotype skull belonged to a mature individual based on hyoid bone histology, but this methodology was questioned by Woodruff et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: An independent study by Christopher T. Griffin and colleagues published later that year argued that the holotype skull of N. lancensis belonged to a mature individual based on histology (microscopic study of the living organism's tissue) of the hyoid bone, but D. Cary Woodruff and colleagues questioned their methodology for hyoid bone histology in 2026.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis specimens possess 15-16 teeth on the upper jaw and 16-18 on the lower jaw, while adult Tyrannosaurus rex has 11-12 upper and 12-14 lower teeth.
facts.quote: Specimens referred to N. lancensis have 15-16 teeth on each side of the maxilla (upper jaw) and 16-18 teeth on each side of the dentary (lower jaw), whereas adult T. rex specimens had 11–12 tooth positions in the upper jaw and 12–14 in the lower.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Carr hypothesized that Nanotyrannus lancensis is a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex based on a decrease in tooth count observed during growth in Gorgosaurus libratus.
facts.quote: Carr showed that, in Gorgosaurus libratus, the number of teeth decreased as the animal grew, and he used this data to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Tsujihi and colleagues noted that tooth count varies significantly between individuals of the same age in Tyrannosaurus and Gorgosaurus, suggesting it may not be strictly linked to growth.
facts.quote: These researchers also noted, however, that both Tyrannosaurus and Gorgosaurus show significant differences in tooth count between individuals of the same age group, and that tooth count may vary on an individual basis unrelated to growth.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis suggested Nanotyrannus specimens exhibit differing levels of cursoriality compared to T. rex, potentially indicating a taxonomic distinction.
facts.quote: A limb proportion analysis published in 2016 suggested that Nanotyrannus specimens have differing levels of cursoriality, cited as a potential difference between N. lancensis and T. rex.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Woodward et al. concluded that Nanotyrannus specimens are ontogenetically immature and likely belong to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: A 2020 study by Holly N. Woodward and colleagues indicated that the specimens referred to Nanotyrannus are ontogenetically immature and found it probable that these specimens belonged to Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Yun (2015) claimed that all distinguishing features of Nanotyrannus are either individual/ontogenetic variations or results of taphonomic distortion.
facts.quote: Yun (2015) claimed that all of the differences used to distinguish Nanotyrannus were individually or ontogenetically variable features, or the products of taphonomic distortion of the bones.

facts.statement: Longrich and Saitta (2024) suggested Nanotyrannus is a distinct taxon potentially outside Tyrannosauridae based on morphology, ontogeny, and phylogeny.
facts.quote: In 2024, Nicholas Longrich and Evan T. Saitta re-examined the holotype and referred specimens of Nanotyrannus. Based on several factors, including differences in morphology, ontogeny, and phylogeny, Longrich and Saitta suggested that Nanotyrannus is a distinct taxon that may fall outside of Tyrannosauridae, based on some of their phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: Voris et al. (2025) argued that Longrich and Saitta's placement of Nanotyrannus outside Tyrannosauridae was caused by immature characteristics and data issues, supporting the view that it is a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Voris et al. (June 2025) suggested that the scoring of Nanotyrannus in a more basal position by Longrich & Saitta (2024) may have been caused by "scoring characteristics related to immaturity" and problematic data sets, supporting the previous interpretation that Nanotyrannus represents a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul (June 2025) supported a basal non-tyrannosaurid position for Nanotyrannus as part of his 'multiple small taxa hypothesis' for theropod diversity.
facts.quote: Later in June 2025, Gregory S. Paul also supported a basal eutyrannosaurian (non-tyrannosaurid) position for Nanotyrannus, emphasizing the validity and distinction of this genus as part of his preferred "multiple small taxa hypothesis" (MSTH) for theropod diversity in the Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli argued that fitting Nanotyrannus into T. rex requires an ontogeny pattern of slow growth, abrupt plateau, and re-growth not seen in any archosaur, contradicting skeletal fusion patterns in the 'Bloody Mary' specimen.
facts.quote: For these specimens to fit within the ontogenetic range of Tyrannosaurus, that taxon would need to spend the first two decades of its life growing slowly before entering an abrupt plateau, and finally re-entering a lengthy growth phase—an ontogeny pattern not seen in any archosaur that contradicts skeletal fusion patterns observed in NCSM 40000.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli concluded that traits like tooth count variation in Nanotyrannus are due to individual variation rather than ontogenetic plasticity.
facts.quote: Furthermore, they concluded that many of the traits commonly cited as ontogenetically plastic (i.e. variations in tooth count) were subject instead to individual variation.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli cited larger arm, wrist, and hand bones in Nanotyrannus compared to Tyrannosaurus as a difference between the two.
facts.quote: Bone proportions were another difference cited by Zanno and Napoli, as some of the arm, wrist, and hand bones of Nanotyrannus are larger than equivalent bones in Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli noted that no known amniotes undergo absolute limb shrinkage, only proportional reduction due to slower limb growth.
facts.quote: There are no amniotes known to the authors that undergo any degree of absolute limb shrinkage, merely instances where limbs grew slower than the rest of the body and became proportionally smaller.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists who previously questioned the validity of Nanotyrannus accepted that the "Bloody Mary" specimen is a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Authors who have authored papers questioning Nanotyrannus validity, such as Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte and David Hone, accepted that the "Bloody Mary" specimen was a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Thomas Carr and Steve Brusatte objected to classifying the juvenile tyrannosaurid BMRP 2002.4.1 "Jane" as Nanotyrannus lethaeus.
facts.quote: Carr and Brusatte objected to the classification of the juvenile tyrannosaurid BMRP 2002.4.1 "Jane" as Nanotyrannus lethaeus

facts.statement: In December 2025, Christopher T. Griffin and colleagues published a study indicating that histology of hyoid bones can assess the ontogenetic maturity of archosaurs.
facts.quote: In December 2025, Christopher T. Griffin and colleagues published the results of a study indicating that histology (microscopic study of the living organism's tissue) of hyoid bones could be used to assess the ontogenetic maturity of archosaurs

facts.statement: After sampling the hyoids of the N. lancensis holotype, researchers concluded it belongs to a mature individual and is a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: After sampling the hyoids of the N. lancensis holotype, the researchers concluded that it belongs to a mature individual, and thus a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid

facts.statement: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm from the anterior tip of the premaxilla to the posterior tip of the quadrate.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm when measured from the anterior (front) tip of the premaxilla to the posterior (rear) tip of the quadrate

facts.statement: The prominent subnarial foramen along the ventral extremity of the premaxilla-maxilla contact point is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: this is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: The quadratojugal and squamosal bones of Nanotyrannus form a long flange.
facts.quote: the quadratojugal and squamosal bones form a long flange

facts.statement: The basitubera of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting the head could be strongly flexed sideways.
facts.quote: the basitubera (muscle attachment sites at the back of the head) of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting that the head could be strongly flexed sideways

facts.statement: The lower jaw bone of Nanotyrannus has a rounded front edge.
facts.quote: The dentary of Nanotyrannus (the tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw), has a rounded anterior margin.

facts.statement: Both species of Nanotyrannus lack chins, a feature present in tyrannosaurids like Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The dentaries of both species lack chins, unlike tyrannosaurids such as Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Each upper front jaw bone of Nanotyrannus held four chisel-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla bore four chisel-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: The upper jaw bones of Nanotyrannus held between fifteen and seventeen teeth, varying by specimen and species.
facts.quote: The maxillae of Nanotyrannus have variable tooth counts: the holotype specimen preserves fifteen, NCSM 40000 has sixteen on the left maxilla and seventeen on the right maxilla, and N. lethaeus appears to have sixteen per maxilla.

facts.statement: The front tooth in each upper jaw of Nanotyrannus was small and similar to the front teeth of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Unlike Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus, but like many other tyrannosauroids, the most anterior tooth of each maxilla was small and resembled those of the premaxillae.

facts.statement: The upper jaw teeth of Nanotyrannus were ziphodont, unlike most tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike most tyrannosaurids, the maxillary teeth were ziphodont.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had between sixteen and eighteen teeth in its lower jaw, more than any tyrannosaurid except Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus has between sixteen and eighteen teeth per dentary, a higher count than in any tyrannosaurid except for Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had approximately twenty neck vertebrae and thirty-five tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column of Nanotyrannus appears to consist of twenty presacral vertebrae (those before the sacrum), and thirty-five caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The second neck vertebra of N. lancensis had a smooth spine, while that of N. lethaeus had small ridges.
facts.quote: The axis of N. lancensis has a straight neural spine (the large projection on the dorsal surface), one lacking any projections on its anterior surface, whereas that of N. lethaeus is crenulate, bearing small ridges.

facts.statement: The tail bones of N. lancensis were hollowed out for air sacs, but those of N. lethaeus were solid.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae of N. lancensis are pneumatised, whereas those of N. lethaeus are not.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had relatively large arms that were more similar to early tyrannosauroids than to later tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The arms of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very large, proportionally more similar to basal tyrannosauroids than to those of tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The lower end of the upper arm bone of Nanotyrannus had five bumps, a feature not found in other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The distal (further from the body) end of the humerus (upper arm bone) of Nanotyrannus bears five tubercles, unlike other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: The hand of Nanotyrannus shared some traits with albertosaurines but differed significantly from tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The manus (hand) is similar in some ways to albertosaurines, though it grossly differs in some regards from tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The first finger bone of Nanotyrannus was nearly twice as large as the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The first phalanx of the first manual digit is nearly twice the size of that of the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had hind legs that were proportionally much longer than those of other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The hind limbs of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very long compared to those of other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the long hind legs of Nanotyrannus indicate a lifestyle adapted for chasing prey rather than ambush hunting.
facts.quote: The extreme proportions of their "hypercursorial" hind limbs may correlate to a different lifestyle from tyrannosaurids, one adapted more toward pursuit predation.

facts.statement: The foot bones of the NCSM 40000 specimen were nearly as long as those of the largest Tyrannosaurus, despite the animal's smaller body size.
facts.quote: Despite its body size being far smaller, the metatarsals of NCSM 40000 are almost as long as those of the very largest Tyrannosaurus specimens.

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was established by Bakker, Currie, and Williams in 1988.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bakker, Currie & Williams, 1988

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Nanotyrannus is Nanotyrannus lancensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Nanotyrannus lancencis

facts.statement: The type species Nanotyrannus lancensis was originally described by Gilmore in 1946.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Gilmore, 1946

facts.statement: A second species, Nanotyrannus lethaeus, was named by Zanno and Napoli in 2025.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Nanotyrannus lethaeus Zanno & Napoli, 2025

facts.statement: Recent studies place Nanotyrannus within the clade Eutyrannosauria and the family Nanotyrannidae, which is the sister group to Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Both recovered Nanotyrannus as a member of the Eutyrannosauria in a new clade deemed the Nanotyrannidae, which is the sister taxon to the Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 68 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which covers parts of Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.

facts.statement: The Hell Creek Formation environment was warm, humid, and swampy, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of this region was warm, humid, and swampy environment, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.

facts.statement: Evidence of intraspecific attack was found on the holotype specimen 'Jane', showing healed puncture wounds believed to be from another juvenile Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Peterson and his team found that Jane's skull showed healed puncture wounds on the upper jaw and snout, which they believe came from another juvenile Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Nanotyrannus had a maximum running speed of 12.57 to 13.82 m/s, nearly twice that of adult T. rex.
facts.quote: In 2020, Alexander Dececchi and colleagues estimated that Jane had a maximum running speed of 12.57 - 13.82 m/s, nearly twice higher than that of adult T. rex with an estimated maximum running speed of 5.81 - 8.07 m/s

facts.statement: It is debated which of the two phylogenetic analyses regarding the relationships within Nanotyrannidae is correct, as further testing and data are required.
facts.quote: The authors noted that further testing and more data would be required to support the results of one analysis over the other.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that the formation of the Western Interior Seaway caused the divergence between tyrannosaurids and nanotyrannids, leading to their separate island continent habitats.
facts.quote: The formation of the seaway may have resulted in their divergence, with tyrannosaurids inhabiting the western island continent of Laramidia, and nanotyrannids inhabiting the eastern island continent of Appalachia.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a medium-sized tyrannosaurid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus es un tiranosauroide de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: Adult Nanotyrannus lancensis may have weighed around 704 kg based on the Bloody Mary specimen.
facts.quote: El N. lancensis adulto pudo haber pesado alrededor de 704 kg, según el espécimen de Bloody Mary.

facts.statement: Mature Nanotyrannus lethaeus could have reached a body mass of approximately 1200 kg.
facts.quote: N. lethaeus, por su parte, era más grande; los individuos maduros pudieron haber alcanzado una masa corporal de aproximadamente 1200 kg.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus measured around 5.5 meters in length and 2 meters in height, about one-third the size of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Solo medía alrededor de 5,5 metros de longitud y 2 de altura, un tercio del tamaño de Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus generally had Cretaceous tyrannosaurid features, including a flat, square head about 60 cm long, sharp claws and teeth, and a heavy body.
facts.quote: En general tenía las características de cualquier tiranosáurido del Cretácico, una cabeza chata y cuadrada con un tamaño cercano a los 60 centímetros de largo, contaba con garras y dientes afilados, así como un cuerpo no liviano.

facts.statement: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus had a thin, low skull with small crests or horns just in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus tenía un cráneo delgado y bajo, y pequeñas crestas o cuernos justo delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: The front upper teeth of Nanotyrannus were not serrated, while the rest were laterally compressed; this condition known as ziphodonty is not observed in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la parte frontal de la mandíbula superior no eran serrados, a diferencia del resto, que a su vez se encontraban comprimidos lateralmente; condición conocida como zifodoncia que no se observa en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had longer legs than contemporaries, suggesting it was a pursuit predator, and possessed forelimbs that were larger both absolutely and proportionally than its relatives.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus tenía patas más largas que los taxones contemporáneos, lo que sugiere que era un depredador de persecución, y poseía extremidades anteriores que eran, tanto en términos absolutos como proporcionales, más grandes que las de sus parientes.

facts.statement: N. lancensis had 14 to 15 teeth on each side of the upper jaw and 16 teeth on each side of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: N. lancensis tenía 14 a 15 dientes de cada lado de la mandíbula superior (maxilar) y 16 dientes en cada lado de la inferior (dentario).

facts.statement: T. rex had 11-12 teeth in its upper jaw and 11-14 in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: T. rex, por su parte, tenía 11-12 dientes posicionados en su mandíbula superior y 11-14 en la inferior.

facts.statement: The exact implications of the difference in tooth number between Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus have been controversial.
facts.quote: Las implicaciones exactas de esta diferencia en el número de dientes ha sido controvertida.

facts.statement: Carr used data showing tooth number decreases as Gorgosaurus libratus develops to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Carr mostró que en Gorgosaurus libratus, el número de dientes decrecía conforme el animal se desarrollaba, y él usó estos datos para apoyar la hipótesis de que N. lancensis es simplemente un T. rex joven.

facts.statement: Scientists studying Tarbosaurus bataar growth found little to no reduction in tooth number during development, even with specimens younger than those of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: El equipo de científicos que estudió el crecimiento en su pariente Tarbosaurus bataar encontró poca o ninguna reducción en el número de dientes en el crecimiento de la especie, incluso aunque disponían de especímenes mucho más jóvenes de lo que serían los de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: In 2013, Carr declared that all differences supporting Nanotyrannus were individual or ontogenetically variable traits or products of bone distortion.
facts.quote: En 2013, Carr declaró que todas las diferencias que afirmaban apoyar a Nanotyrannus resultaron ser características individuales u ontogenéticamente variables o productos de distorsión de los huesos.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Manabu Sakomoto commented that the conclusion regarding limb proportions is likely affected by small sample size and does not necessarily reflect taxonomic distinction.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Manabu Sakomoto ha comentado que esta conclusión probablemente se ve afectada por el bajo tamaño de la muestra, y la discrepancia no necesariamente refleja la distinción taxonómica.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus morphology combines features of basal tyrannosauroids like Moros and Xiongguanlong with more derived tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: La morfología de Nanotyrannus combina características de tiranosauroides más basales, como Moros y Xiongguanlong, con tiranosáuridos más derivados.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic hypothesis suggests Nanotyrannus is closely related to Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus and descended from an Appalachian tyrannosaur lineage that migrated to Laramidia as the Western Interior Seaway regressed.
facts.quote: una hipótesis filogenética sugiere relaciones cercanas con Appalachiosaurus y Dryptosaurus dentro de este clado, y que Nanotyrannus descendió de un linaje de tiranosaurios de los Apalaches que migraron al otro continente insular de América del Norte, Laramidia, con la regresión del Mar interior occidental.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalog number CMNH 7541, was discovered by Charles W. Gilmore in 1942 and described in 1946 as Gorgosaurus lancensis.
facts.quote: Representado por un pequeño cráneo, número de catálogo CMNH 7541, descubierto por Charles W. Gilmore en 1942 y descrito en 1946 como un espécimen de Gorgosaurus lancensis

facts.statement: The type locality was later corrected to the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la localidad tipo se ha corregido posteriormente a la Formación Hell Creek

facts.statement: In 1988, the specimen was redescribed by Robert T. Bakker, Phil Currie, and Michael Williams.
facts.quote: En 1988, el espécimen fue redescrito por Robert T. Bakker, Phil Currie, y Michael Williams

facts.statement: The etymology of the name comes from the Greek words nanos, meaning dwarf or pygmy, and tyrannos, meaning king.
facts.quote: Posteriormente se aclaró que la etimología proviene de las palabras griegas νάνος (nanos), que significa «enano» o «pigmeo», y τύραννος (tyrannos), que significa «rey»

facts.statement: The possibility that the holotype represented a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex was first suggested by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1965.
facts.quote: La posibilidad de que el holotipo representara un Tyrannosaurus rex juvenil fue sugerida por primera vez por Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky en 1965

facts.statement: A detailed analysis of the specimen by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated that it was indeed a juvenile.
facts.quote: Un detallado análisis del espécimen hecho por Thomas Carr en 1999 indicó que este espécimen era de hecho un juvenil

facts.statement: This view was strengthened by the discovery in 2001 of a new Nanotyrannus specimen nicknamed "Jane", catalog number BMRP 2002.4.1.
facts.quote: especialmente desde el descubrimiento en 2001 de un nuevo espécimen de Nanotyrannus, apodado "Jane", número de catálogo BMRP 2002.4.1

facts.statement: In a 2016 article, Joshua David Schmerge proposed that Nanotyrannus is a valid genus based on specimen BMRP 2002.4.1, due to a tooth groove not seen in known Tyrannosaurus rex specimens.
facts.quote: Joshua David Schmerge propuso en un artículo de 2016, que Nanotyrannus es un género válido basado en el espécimen BMRP 2002.4.1, debido a su surco dentario que no se ve en especímenes conocidos de Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: In the same year, Carr and associates wrote a separate document claiming that the presence or absence of a tooth groove does not clarify the validity of Nanotyrannus or its phylogenetic position among tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: En el mismo año, Carr y sus asociados escribieron un documento separado que afirmó que la presencia o ausencia de un surco dentario no aclara la validez de Nanotyrannus o su posición filogenética entre los tirannosauroides

facts.statement: In a 2020 article, Carr re-examined CMNH 7541 and found it fit the expected ontogenetic variation of the taxon.
facts.quote: Carr estudió CMNH 7541 nuevamente en un artículo de 2020 sobre la historia de crecimiento de Tyrannosaurus, encontrando que se ajustaba a la variación ontogenética esperada del taxón

facts.statement: Others, such as Peter Larson, continue to support a separate genus for Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: Otros, como Peter Larson, continúan apoyando un género separado para Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: The scientific study of Jane by Bakker, Larson, and Currie may help determine if Nanotyrannus is a separate genus, a new tyrannosaurid genus and species, or simply a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: El estudio científico de Jane, que publicarán Bakker, Larson, y Currie, puede ayudar a determinar si Nanotyrannus pertenece a un género propio, es un nuevo género y especie de tiranosáurido, o simplemente un Tyrannosaurus rex joven

facts.statement: However, there are subtle and potentially significant differences in the shape of the teeth, maxillae, and dentaries.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, existen diferencias sutiles y potencialmente significativas en la forma de los dientes, maxilares y dentarios

facts.statement: In 2001, a more complete juvenile tyrannosaur nicknamed "Jane" (accession number BMRP 2002.4.1) was discovered, which was suggested to belong to the same species as the original Nanotyrannus specimen.
facts.quote: En 2001, se descubrió un tiranosaurio juvenil más completo (apodado "Jane", número de acceso BMRP 2002.4.1), que se sugirió pertenecía a la misma especie que el espécimen original de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Several paleontologists, including Currie and Williams, who previously supported N. lancensis as a valid species, viewed the discovery of "Jane" as confirmation that Nanotyrannus was actually a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Varios paleontólogos que previamente habían publicado opiniones a favor de N. lancensis como especie válida, entre ellos Currie y Williams, vieron el descubrimiento de "Jane" como una confirmación de que Nanotyrannus era, de hecho, un T. rex juvenil.

facts.statement: Peter Larson continued to support the hypothesis that Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct but closely related species and argued that Stygivenator (LACM 28471), generally considered a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex, could be a younger specimen of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: Peter Larson siguió apoyando la hipótesis de que Nanotyrannus lancensis era una especie distinta pero estrechamente relacionada, y también argumentó que Stygivenator (LACM 28471), que generalmente se considera un ejemplar juvenil de Tyrannosaurus rex, podría ser un espécimen más joven de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: In late 2011, news reports covered the 2006 discovery of a nearly complete tyrannosaur specimen found alongside a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: A finales de 2011, se hicieron informes de noticias sobre el descubrimiento en 2006, de un nuevo espécimen de tiranosaurio prácticamente completo encontrado junto con un cerátopsido.

facts.statement: Robert Bakker and Pete Larson studied the specimens at the site, identifying the ceratopsian as Triceratops and the tyrannosaur as Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: Los especímenes fueron estudiados por Robert Bakker y Pete Larson en el sitio, quienes identificaron al ceratopsiano como Triceratops y al tiranosaurio como Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Bloody Mary" has arms nearly 3 feet long, and its hand bones are said to be one and a half times longer than those of the T. rex specimen "Sue".
facts.quote: El espécimen, apodado "Bloody Mary", tiene brazos de casi 3 pies de largo, y se dice que los huesos de la mano son una vez y media más largos que los del espécimen de T. rex "Sue".

facts.statement: In 2020, the Montana Supreme Court ruled that ownership of the specimen should be granted to the landowners, Mary Anne and Lige Murray, who agreed to sell the fossils to a US museum.
facts.quote: En 2020, el Tribunal Supremo de Montana dictaminó que la propiedad del espécimen debía ser otorgada a los propietarios del terreno, Mary Anne y Lige Murray, quienes acordaron vender los fósiles a un museo estadounidense.

facts.statement: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences acquired the fossil in 2020 and subsequently built an additional research laboratory to prepare, study, and exhibit the specimens.
facts.quote: El Museo de Ciencias Naturales de Carolina del Norte adquirió el fósil en 2020 y, posteriormente, construyó un laboratorio de investigación adicional para preparar , estudiar y exhibir los especímenes.

facts.statement: They identified this specimen as a mature individual of Nanotyrannus and provided various evidence supporting the validity of this genus.
facts.quote: Identificaron este espécimen como un individuo de Nanotyrannus con el esqueleto maduro y aportaron diversas pruebas que respaldaban la validez de este género.

facts.statement: They also described a second species, N. lethaeus, based on the Jane specimen, due to notable differences between it and N. lancensis.
facts.quote: También describieron una segunda especie, N. lethaeus, basándose en el espécimen Jane, debido a las notables diferencias entre este y N. lancensis.

facts.statement: The specific name of the second species, lethaeus, comes from Latin and is the adjective of Lethe, referring to the river Lethe of Greco-Roman mythology, which flows through the underworld (often equated with hell).
facts.quote: El nombre específico de la segunda especie, lethaeus, proviene del latín y es el adjetivo de Lete, en referencia al río Lete de la mitología grecorromana, que fluye a través del inframundo (a menudo equiparado al infierno).

facts.statement: Some scientists have defended the validity of Nanotyrannus lancensis based on differences in tooth count.
facts.quote: La principal diferencia que algunos científicos han utilizado para defender la validez de Nanotyrannus lancensis radica en el número de dientes.

facts.statement: The implications of the tooth count difference between Nanotyrannus and adult T. rex have not been universally accepted.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, las implicaciones exactas de esta diferencia en el número de dientes no han sido aceptadas universalmente.

facts.statement: The presence of a small foramen in the quadratojugal is cited as a difference supporting the validity of N. lancensis.
facts.quote: Otra diferencia citada en apoyo de la validez de N. lancensis es la presencia de un pequeño foramen en el cuadratoyugal.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Holly N. Woodward and colleagues indicated that specimens attributed to Nanotyrannus are ontogenetically immature and likely belong to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2020 realizado por Holly N. Woodward y sus colegas indicó que los especímenes atribuidos a Nanotyrannus son ontogenéticamente inmaduros y halló probable que pertenecieran a Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: In 2024, Nicholas Longrich and Evan T. Saitta reexamined the holotype and referred specimens of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: En 2024, Nicholas Longrich y Evan T. Saitta reexaminaron el holotipo y los especímenes referidos de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Longrich and Saitta concluded that tyrannosaurid diversity before the K-Pg extinction was greater than previously believed.
facts.quote: Por lo que la diversidad de tiranosáuridos antes de la extinción K-Pg es mayor de lo que se creía anteriormente.

facts.statement: Paul argued that N. lancensis has been treated as a wastebasket taxon likely comprising fossils of multiple taxa.
facts.quote: afirmó que N. lancensis ha sido tratado como un taxón cajón de sastre que probablemente comprende fósiles de múltiples taxones.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli concluded that specimen Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), assigned to N. lethaeus, died between the ages of 8 and 14 years.
facts.quote: En el mismo artículo, Zanno y Napoli concluyeron que otro espécimen de Nanotyrannus , Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), al que asignaron a N. lethaeus , murió entre los 8 y los 14 años de edad.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli noted that no known amniote experiences absolute reduction of limbs, only cases where limbs grew more slowly than the rest of the body and became proportionally smaller.
facts.quote: Los autores no conocen ningún amniota que experimente algún grado de reducción absoluta de las extremidades, sino simplemente casos en los que las extremidades crecieron más lentamente que el resto del cuerpo y se volvieron proporcionalmente más pequeñas.

facts.statement: The article by Zanno and Napoli led some previously skeptical paleontologists to accept Nanotyrannus as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: El artículo de Zanno y Napoli ha llevado a algunos paleontólogos, antes escépticos respecto a Nanotyrannus, a aceptarlo como un taxón válido.

facts.statement: Carr opined that Nanotyrannus should be considered a species within the genus Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Carr opinó que Nanotyrannus debería considerarse una especie dentro del género Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Gilmore classified Nanotyrannus lancensis as a species of Gorgosaurus in 1946.
facts.quote: Gilmore en 1946 concluyó que Nanotyrannus lancensis era una especie de Gorgosaurus.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli published phylogenetic analyses in 2025 that identified Nanotyrannus as a member of Eutyrannosauria within a new clade called Nanotyrannidae.
facts.quote: En su artículo de 2025, Zanno y Napoli realizaron dos análisis filogenéticos utilizando un extenso conjunto de datos novedoso centrado en el muestreo de tiranosauroides.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the exact resolution of taxa within Nanotyrannidae and their relationships, as different analyses yield conflicting results.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la resolución exacta de los taxones dentro de Nanotyrannidae y en relación con ella difiere entre ambos análisis.

facts.statement: Peterson and colleagues found evidence of an intraspecific attack on the specimen "Jane," which was previously thought to be a juvenile Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Joseph Peterson y sus colegas hallaron evidencia de un ataque intraespecífico en Jane, que en ese entonces se creía que era una Tyrannosaurus juvenil.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils have been found in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus se encontró en la Formación Hell Creek, que abarca partes de los actuales Montana, Dakota del Sur, Dakota del Norte y Wyoming.

facts.statement: The sedimentary environment of the Hell Creek Formation was warm, humid, and swampy, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: El ambiente de sedimentación de esta región era cálido, húmedo y pantanoso, lo que refleja condiciones marítimas a subtropicales.

facts.statement: Average temperatures in the Hell Creek Formation environment ranged between 11.3 and 11.6 degrees Celsius.
